description:
Three implicit identities under the 'exact' claim: capture↔review source-path string equality (F8 — nil source and path mismatch both collapse to uncovered), no_debug_info_mfas conflating three states while sitting in the closure pct denominator (F11), and two independently derived module-scope caches where a file_map miss silently deletes lines from payload AND remainder (F23). Also F18: missing :attribution renders as :exact — unknown provenance must render unqualified. Specify path identity (repo-root-relative, normalized both sides), classify unresolvable sources as their own partition, single-source the module scope + surface misses as meta.unmapped_modules. Report Theme 4.

---

## Orchestrator scoping (synthesized 2026-07-25 by /orchestrate-epic from verified code analysis)

## specled_-dn4.5 — Specify the capture↔review identity joins (F8, F11, F23, F18)

**Advances:** `specled.coverage_capture`, `specled.triangulation`, `specled.spec_review`

Matched obligations:

- `specled.coverage_capture.envelope_meta` (`.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md:502-513`) — the requirement that enumerates `meta.boundary` / `meta.unhooked_modules` / `meta.unattributed`; adding `meta.unmapped_modules` co-changes here, plus scenario `specled.coverage_capture.scenario.envelope_meta_tolerant_read` (:833-842).
- `specled.coverage_capture.formatter_auditor` (:528-542) — owns the remainder computation the file_map miss corrupts.
- `specled.triangulation.per_test_requirement_reach` (`.spec/specs/triangulation.spec.md:205-218`) — literally the requirement that says `no_debug_info_mfas` must not silently proxy; the three-state conflation and the path-identity join both live under it. Scenario `specled.triangulation.scenario.per_test_reach_line_intersection` (:319-330).
- `specled.spec_review.coverage_tab_v2_envelope_data_layer` (`.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md:383-413`) and `specled.spec_review.coverage_observed_approximate_qualifier` (:320-332) — F18's "missing `:attribution` must render unqualified" is a rendering obligation under these two. Scenario `specled.spec_review.coverage_qualifies_exact_up_to_escaped` (:709-720).

**Primary files, per finding:**

*F8 — path identity.* Both sides derive paths from `module_info(:compile)[:source]` but neither normalizes to repo-root-relative:

- capture: `lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex:268-282` `defp source_file/1` (returns the raw compile-time absolute path, `nil` on any failure) feeding `build_file_map/1` at :241-243.
- review: `lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex:396-421` `defp module_source_index/1` + `defp module_source_file/1`, matched against record `:file` via `defp normalize_path/1` at :710-714 — which only does `String.trim_leading("./")`. Not a repo-root normalization.
- the collapse: `defp tests_hitting_mfa(_per_test, nil, _mfa_lines), do: []` at `coverage_triangulation.ex:349` — a `nil` source silently yields "no test hit this MFA", i.e. **uncovered**, indistinguishable from a genuine miss. A path mismatch reaches the same verdict via the `Map.get(t.lines_by_file, source_norm, MapSet.new())` default at :355.
- contrast: `lib/specled_ex/coverage/aggregate.ex:184` maps to repo-relative, so aggregate and per_test lanes disagree on path shape.

*F11 — `no_debug_info_mfas` conflates three states and sits in the pct denominator.*

- `lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex:297-347` `defp requirement_per_test_reach/4`. The three states all funnel into `ndi`: (a) `Map.get(line_index, mod, :no_debug_info)` matching `:no_debug_info` at :305-307 — which **also swallows "module absent from line_index entirely"** via the default; (b) `Map.fetch(fun_index, {fun, arity})` returning `:error` at :310-312.
- denominator: `closure_mfa_count: length(closure_mfas)` at :340 counts every closure MFA including the `no_debug` ones, while `executed_mfa_count: length(covered_sorted)` at :341 cannot. `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:550-556` `v2_requirement_entry/2` then computes `Float.round(r.executed_mfa_count / r.closure_mfa_count * 100, 2)` — so unresolvable MFAs depress the percentage as if untested.
- the MfaKey parse failure at :331-332 is a **fourth** state, currently folded into `uncovered`.

*F23 — two module-scope caches; a file_map miss deletes lines twice.*

- cache 1: `formatter.ex:241-243` `build_file_map/1`. Cache 2: `coverage_triangulation.ex:396-405` `module_source_index/1`.
- the double deletion: `formatter.ex:248-258` `defp compact_hits_to_files/2` drops any module whose `file_map` entry is `nil` (`nil -> acc` at :252). It is called **twice** in `flush/1`: at :302 for the unattributed remainder and at :390 for the payload records. A module missing from the map therefore vanishes from both — the very remainder that is supposed to be the safety net.
- new `meta.unmapped_modules` lands in the `meta` construction at `formatter.ex:344-349`.

*F18 — missing `:attribution` renders as `:exact`.* Five verified sites, all `Map.get(…, :attribution, :exact)`:

- `lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex:2035` (`rollup_qualifier_suffix/1`, :2032-2043)
- `:2050` (`rollup_qualifier_title_suffix/1`, :2047-2067)
- `:3064` (`render_attribution_qualifier/2`, :3063-3078)
- `:3123` (`reached_by_tests_title/1`, :3122-3135)
- `:3152` (`self_verified_qualifier_label/1`, :3151-3156)
- the producer that legitimately omits the key: `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:383-389` `maybe_put_attribution/4` adds `:attribution` **only** for `:ok_per_test`; `per_test_attribution/1` at :391-396 has an `_ -> :exact` catch-all clause. So a subject map built any other way arrives keyless and renders "exact".

**Allowed touches (globs):**

- `lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex`
- `lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex`
- `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex`
- `lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex`
- `lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex` (only if `meta.unmapped_modules` needs envelope validation / a `Store` reader beside `degraded_reasons/1`)
- `test/specled_ex/coverage/formatter_test.exs`
- `test/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation_test.exs`
- `test/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure_test.exs`
- `test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs`
- `.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md`
- `.spec/specs/triangulation.spec.md`
- `.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md`
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.*.md` (a new ADR — see intent)
- `.spec/realization_hashes.json`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

**Out of Scope (files):** `lib/specled_ex/coverage/boundary.ex`, `lib/specled_ex/coverage.ex`, `lib/specled_ex/coverage/snapshot.ex`, `lib/specled_ex/coverage/mfa_lines.ex`, `lib/specled_ex/coverage/aggregate.ex` (unless the repo-relative normalization is deliberately single-sourced there — then say so and add it), `lib/mix/tasks/**`, `.spec/specs/package.spec.md`, `.spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md`.

**Out of Scope (intent):**

- This is the one ticket in the epic that legitimately **adds** requirements (path identity, the unresolvable-source partition, `meta.unmapped_modules`). Additions are append-only-safe; **do not weaken or delete** `per_test_requirement_reach` or `envelope_meta` text to fit the implementation.
- The claim being repaired is honesty, not coverage: a newly-surfaced unresolvable partition will *lower* reported percentages. That is the intended outcome — do not compensate.
- Because this changes what "exact" means at the review surface, an ADR under `.spec/decisions/` is warranted (the existing `specled.decision.per_test_sync_boundary.md` is the natural companion). Do not silently reinterpret the shipped claim.
- Do not fold the five `attribution` sites into one helper here — that is dn4.9's `attribution_copy/1` item; fix the **default** at all five, leave the refactor to dn4.9.

**Verification:**

- `mix test test/specled_ex/coverage/formatter_test.exs test/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation_test.exs test/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure_test.exs test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs test/mix/tasks/spec_cover_test_test.exs`
- `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`, then `mix spec.check`
- Stubs, all **`execute: true`**: `coverage_capture.spec.md:943-947` (`envelope_meta`), :948-953 (`formatter_auditor`); `triangulation.spec.md:359-368` (`per_test_requirement_reach`); `spec_review.spec.md:805-810` — `kind: command, target: mix test test/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure_test.exs` covering `coverage_tab_v2_envelope_data_layer`, and :806-820 — `target: mix test test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs` covering `coverage_observed_approximate_qualifier` + `coverage_file_level_proxy_qualifier`.

**Overlap risk:** The widest-reaching ticket.

- `lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex` — **dn4.2** rewrites `flush/1`, whose `meta` block and both `compact_hits_to_files/2` call sites dn4.5 edits. Sharpest conflict in the epic; sequence dn4.2 before dn4.5.
- `lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex` — **dn4.9** (fold `group_records_with_lines/1` at :367-391 into `group_records_by_test/1` at :433; `MapSet.disjoint?/2` at :357; non-loading source resolution at :407-421 — the exact function F8 rewrites).
- `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex` — **dn4.6** (F12 hoists the `per_test_requirement_reach/3` call at :511 out of the per-subject loop).
- `lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex` — **dn4.8** (`# covers:` comments at :2025, :2719, :3058, :3059, :3137 if F39 renames ids), **dn4.9** (`attribution_copy/1`).
- `.spec/specs/triangulation.spec.md` — **specled_-cz0** (see dn4.8 below).
- `.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md` — **dn4.8** (F36 scenario, F39 id renames).

## Semantic checks

Every claim below was mutation-checked: I reverted the specific behavior, ran the suite, and recorded which assertion fires. Worktree restored to clean after each probe.

### F8 — path identity (capture and review)

Both sides now normalize to a repo-root-relative identity:
- capture: formatter.ex source_file/1 -> repo_relative_path/1 (formatter.ex:274-281)
- review: coverage_triangulation.ex module_source_file/1 and group_records_with_lines/1 -> repo_relative_source_path/1 (coverage_triangulation.ex:436-445)

NOT single-sourced — two private copies in two modules — but the bodies are logically identical (File.cwd! |> Path.expand; Path.expand(path, root); starts_with?(root <> "/") then Path.relative_to/2, else nil). The ticket permitted "single-sourced OR provably identical", so this clears the bar. Flagging the drift risk under Notes.

The masquerade is closed on the axis the finding named: the tests_hitting_mfa(_per_test, nil, _mfa_lines) -> [] clause is DELETED. A nil/unresolvable source can no longer reach the intersection at all — it is intercepted by Map.fetch(source_by_module, mod) => :error and routed to the unresolvable partition. Verified by mutation, not by reading.

Would-fail-if (capture): revert repo_relative_path/1 in source_file/1 => 2 failures in formatter_test.exs — "assert file == Path.relative_to_cwd(source)" and "refute Path.type(record.file) == :absolute".
Would-fail-if (review): revert repo_relative_source_path/1 in module_source_file/1 => 3 failures in coverage_closure_test.exs, incl. "per_test mode: repo-relative record paths join an absolute compile source path" (assert req.covered_mfas == [@fixture_a_mfa]).
Seams: FixtureA's real compile-time absolute source joined against a Path.relative_to_cwd record path — a genuine absolute-to-relative join, not a string fixture.

### F11 — no_debug_info_mfas three-state conflation + denominator

All four states are now genuinely distinguishable, and each is INDIVIDUALLY pinned (I mutated them one at a time, not as a group):

- module absent from line_index -> unresolvable_source_mfas. Would-fail-if reverted to the old Map.get(line_index, mod, :no_debug_info) default => 2 failures ("a closure module absent from the line index is unresolvable, not no-debug or uncovered").
- module present but :no_debug_info -> stays in no_debug_info_mfas. Held constant across all four probes; every partition test also asserts the complementary "no_debug_info_mfas == []".
- MFA absent from fun_index -> unresolvable. Would-fail-if routed back to ndi => 1 failure.
- MfaKey parse failure (the fourth state, previously folded into uncovered) -> unresolvable. Would-fail-if routed back to uncovered => 1 failure ("an unparseable closure MFA is unresolvable rather than uncovered").
- unresolved compile source -> unresolvable. Would-fail-if routed back to uncovered => 1 failure.

DENOMINATOR — the specific question asked. closure_mfa_count is still length(closure_mfas) (coverage_triangulation.ex:351), executed_mfa_count is still length(covered_sorted) (:352), and the pct formula at coverage_closure.ex:571 is untouched. Unresolvable MFAs stay in the denominator and contribute zero to the numerator.

This is documented in the SPEC, not only the code: specled.triangulation.per_test_unresolvable_source_partition states "Its MFAs remain in closure_mfa_count and contribute zero to executed_mfa_count; they shall not be removed from the coverage-percentage denominator." The ADR repeats it.

Honesty invariant — NO COMPENSATION FOUND. I grepped every closure_mfa_count / executed_mfa_count site in lib/ and mutation-tested the wrong fix explicitly: changing closure_mfa_count to "length(closure_mfas) - length(unresolvable)" => 2 failures (assert req.closure_mfa_count == 1, in two separate tests). The reclassification moves MFAs only between buckets that were already non-executed and already in the denominator, so the net effect on reported pct is unchanged-or-lower, never higher.

### F23 — two module-scope caches; file_map miss deleting lines twice

Module scope: both compact_hits_to_files/2 call sites in flush/1 (payload via records_for_inventory/3, remainder via unattributed_files) consume the same state.file_map built once by build_file_map/1. The spec now PINS that ("Boundary payload and remainder compaction shall reuse the same suite-start module-to-source map") — note this property already held before dn4.5; the ticket's contribution here is the spec text plus the disclosure, not a code change to the sharing.

Misses now surface: meta.unmapped_modules is computed over both attributed_hits and unattributed_hits (formatter.ex:317-324) and emitted via maybe_put at :372.
Would-fail-if: delete the maybe_put(:unmapped_modules, ...) line => "assert envelope.meta.unmapped_modules == [unmapped]" fails.
Seams: the formatter test drives a real flush with two hit modules — Fixture (resolvable) and UnloadableCoverageModule (not) — through boundary and run-total hits.

IMPORTANT interpretive point for the reviewer: the remainder is NOT restored as a safety net. An unmapped module's LINES are still absent from both payload and remainder; what changed is that the loss is now named. The test asserts this deliberately ("refute Enum.any?(meta[:unattributed], fn {_f, lines} -> unmapped_line in lines end)"), and the spec/ADR state it explicitly ("their lines shall not be fabricated under another file"). I judge this the correct reading of the finding — fabricating a file key would be a stronger claim, which is what the epic exists to prevent — but it does mean the ticket's "the remainder no longer loses the same modules the payload does" framing is satisfied by disclosure, not by retention.

### F18 — missing :attribution must render unqualified

All five sites changed, and "unqualified" genuinely means absent — empty string from the render functions, nil label from self_verified_qualifier_label/1 (which then suppresses the whole span) — not a substituted weaker qualifier. Production is unaffected: maybe_put_attribution/4 still always sets the key for :ok_per_test, so only hand-built/legacy maps take the new path.

There IS a keyless-subject-map test ("keyless per-test reach stays unqualified across closure, reached-by, self-verified, and rollup surfaces", html_test.exs:1452) and I mutation-checked each of the five sites SEPARATELY rather than trusting the whole-file revert, because a refute short-circuits and can mask siblings. Results:

- rollup_qualifier_suffix/1 + rollup_qualifier_title_suffix/1 — PINNED. Restoring the :exact default on those two alone => fails on "refute badge_html =~ \"exact within chained windows\"".
- render_attribution_qualifier/2 — PINNED. Fails on "refute tab_html =~ \"cov-closure-attribution-note\"".
- self_verified_qualifier_label/1 — PINNED. Fails on "refute tab_html =~ \"cov-closure-self-verified-note\"".
- reached_by_tests_title/1 — **NOT PINNED**. See Gaps.

## Verdict

FAIL — one gap. The implementation is correct on all four findings and every gate is green; the defect is a missing assertion, not wrong behavior. One of the five F18 sites can have its pre-fix default restored with the entire 1226-test suite passing, which is precisely the failure mode this ticket's own gate checks exist to prevent.

## Gaps

GAP 1 (blocking) — reached_by_tests_title/1 (lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex:3139-3155) is an unpinned F18 site. A silently restored :exact default there survives the full suite.

Mutation performed: replaced the head

    defp reached_by_tests_title(%{attribution: attribution} = subject_reach)
         when attribution in [:exact, :degraded_unhooked] do
      case Map.get(subject_reach || %{}, :attribution) do

with the pre-fix form

    defp reached_by_tests_title(subject_reach) when is_map(subject_reach) do
      case Map.get(subject_reach || %{}, :attribution, :exact) do

Result: mix test (FULL suite) => 3 properties, 1226 tests, 0 failures. Zero failures. This is the same shape as the dn4.6 residual that gate checks a-d were written to protect.

Why the existing test misses it — two independent reasons, both need to hold for the assertion to work:

1. The other three tab-surface sites are caught by CLASS refutes (cov-closure-attribution-note, cov-closure-self-verified-note) because their whole span disappears when unqualified. reached_by_tests_title/1's output is not a span — it is the value of the title= attribute on <span class="cov-reached-by-tests-label">, which renders UNCONDITIONALLY (html.ex:3125 and :3135). Only the attribute value changes, from title="" to the full claim. No class refute can observe it.

2. The one text refute that could have caught it, "refute tab_html =~ \"exact within chained windows\"" (html_test.exs:1484), misses by one word. The title returns @exact_up_to_escaped_title, whose wording is "Per-test attribution is exact within DISCLOSED chained windows: ...".
